title: Weekly Cybersecurity Newsletter — Top 50 Cybersecurity Stories of the Week
content_md: Welcome to this edition of the CyberPress weekly cybersecurity newsletter your cybersecurity bulletin covering the 50 most important stories from September 14 to 18, 2026, organized day by day. AI stayed at the center: agentic ransomware went autonomous, PROMPTFLUX rewrote its own code with Gemini, and autonomous agents harvested tens of thousands of cloud secrets. Exploitation ran hot too Check Point, Cisco Secure Email Gateway and FortiGate flaws came under active attack, Chrome 153 patched 42 bugs, and a Revolut breach exposed passports and KYC selfies. Everything below is curated into one weekly cybersecurity newsletter so you can scan the week in minutes and click through to the full analysis. In this cybersecurity bulletin: Friday (8) · Thursday (10) · Wednesday (16) · Tuesday (8) · Monday (8) FRIDAY · SEPTEMBER 18, 2026 8 stories 1 AI Agentic Ransomware Lets AI Agents Execute Cyberattacks Without Human Operators Agentic ransomware now lets AI agents execute cyberattacks without human operators. It marks a worrying step toward fully autonomous extortion. 2 AI PROMPTFLUX Uses Google Gemini to Rewrite Its Malware Code Every Hour PROMPTFLUX uses Google Gemini to rewrite its own malware code every hour. Constant AI-driven mutation helps it slip past signature-based defenses. 3 MALWARE MovieReaper Gives Hackers 21 Commands to Steal and Manipulate Files on Windows PCs MovieReaper gives hackers 21 commands to steal and manipulate files on Windows PCs.
